title: B196 — Guard the Dagster watchdog: budgets must match schedules, and a never-run job must alert
description:
## Why

`dagster-freshness-check` (`k8s/dagster/freshness.yaml`, every 30m) alerts per Dagster job when the last run FAILED or no success lands within a per-job budget. Two gaps, both found shipping B194 (2026-09-27):

1. **Budgets drift from schedules with nothing going red.** `weyland_catalog_job`, `weyland_timeseries_job` and `datahub_catalog_emit_job` moved to nightly on 2026-08-07, but their budgets stayed 6–8h. For **seven weeks** they fired false `DagsterJobStale` alerts every 30 minutes, drowning real ones. Fixed by hand 2026-09-27 (30h). `scripts/check-cron-freshness-budgets.sh` covers k8s CronJobs only; nothing compares the watchdog's `threshold_for` table with the Dagster `ScheduleDefinition`s.
2. **A job that has never run is invisible.** The watchdog's SQL lists only jobs with at least one row in `runs`, so a monitored job whose schedule never fires (or ships STOPPED) never alerts. Same absence-as-success class as the B135 `absent()` companion for CronJobs. B194's new `linear_backup_job` had exactly this state until its first scheduled run.

## Scope

1. A repo guard (`scripts/check-dagster-watchdog-budgets.sh` + bats, wired into `repo-guards`) that parses every `ScheduleDefinition` (cron, name, job, `default_status`) and the watchdog's `threshold_for` table, and fails when: a RUNNING scheduled job has no budget; a budget is below \~1.25× the cron's interval; a budget names a job that no longer exists.
2. In the watchdog: for every job with a budget but NO row in `runs`, fire `DagsterJobNeverRan` — except jobs whose schedule ships STOPPED, recorded in an explicit accepted list with the reason (the ai_session pattern already in the file).
3. Document both in the DoD Pillar 6 "Triggered" bullet and `docs/runbooks/` (the watchdog's home).

## Technical context

| Where | What | Role |
| -- | -- | -- |
| repo | `nodes/mother/lab/weyland-platform/k8s/dagster/freshness.yaml` | watchdog (`threshold_for` table + SQL) — changed |
| repo | `services/weyland-dagster/weyland_pipeline/{definitions.py,schedules/__init__.py}` | ScheduleDefinitions — read by the guard |
| repo | `scripts/check-cron-freshness-budgets.sh` | sibling guard for CronJobs — the pattern to follow |
| CI | `.woodpecker.yml` `repo-guards` | runs the new guard |

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The guard passes on the current repo and FAILS (by named reason, not bare exit) on: a budget under the cron interval, a RUNNING schedule with no budget, a budget for a deleted job — each proven by a bats case.
- [ ] Reverting one of the 2026-09-27 fixes (e.g. catalog back to 28800) makes the guard fail naming `weyland_catalog_job`.
- [ ] A budgeted job with no runs fires `DagsterJobNeverRan`; an accepted STOPPED job does not.
- [ ] Exit codes follow the lab convention: 1 = defect found, 2 = the guard could not run.

## Edge cases & failure modes

* Schedules generated by factories (`build_domain_jobs`) — the guard must see them, or state it can't (exit 2), never pass by missing them.
* Cron parsing: weekly/monthly crons need their real interval; an unparseable cron is exit 2.
* `default_status` STOPPED in code but RUNNING in the UI (the datasets land schedules) — code is what the guard can read; the accepted list states the live exception.

## Out of scope

* Moving to Dagster's native run-status sensor (broken on this Dagster line, dagster#21526 — revisit on a major upgrade).
* Re-tuning budgets beyond the \~2× cadence convention.

Relates B194 (found shipping it), B94 (the per-job watchdog), B135 (the CronJob freshness guards). Detail: [https://github.com/edtbl76/weyland-lab/blob/main/docs/backlog.md](<https://github.com/edtbl76/weyland-lab/blob/main/docs/backlog.md>)
